title: What is Git?
overview: Git is a distributed version control system used to track changes in code and manage software development projects.

title: Why Use Git?
overview: Git helps developers manage code history, collaborate with teams, and restore previous versions of projects.

example.title: Git Benefits
example.content:
✔ Version history
✔ Team collaboration
✔ Code backup
✔ Change tracking

title: How Git Works
overview: Git stores snapshots of project changes and allows developers to move between different versions of their code.

title: Git Repository
overview: A Git repository stores all project files, history, branches, and commits.

example.title: Repository Types
example.content:
Local Repository:
Stored on computer

Remote Repository:
Stored online

title: Git vs GitHub
overview: Git is a version control tool, while GitHub is a platform that hosts Git repositories online.

example.title: Difference
example.content:
Git:
Version Control System

GitHub:
Online Repository Platform

title: Topic Summary
overview: You learned what Git is, why it is used, how it works, and the difference between Git and GitHub.

example.title: Quick Revision
example.content:
✔ Git tracks changes.
✔ Repository stores history.
✔ GitHub hosts repositories online.
